track: B - quarter-BPS dyons on K3 x T2 (DMVV product; Dabholkar-Murthy-Zagier)
tier: B (exact rational arithmetic with negative controls); conjecture/literature-identification claims marked separately; nothing here is 'proved'
commands_to_reproduce: python theta_forms.py 22   # builds A,B,E4,E6,Delta and the c(D) table, QMAX=22

e_K3_from_c0_plus_2cm1.note: e(K3) = c(0) + 2*c(-1); expect 24 (Euler characteristic of K3) but this is COMPUTED not assumed

expected_from_literature_UNVERIFIED.note: from memory, Dabholkar-Murthy-Zagier / Eguchi-Ooguri-Taormina K3 elliptic genus table

2_part1_euler_numbers.honesty_note: This q^0,y=1 restriction of DMVV collapses ANALYTICALLY (derived above, not assumed) to prod_r (1-p^r)^{-kappa*(c0+2*cm1)}, i.e. a single linear equation kappa*(c0+2*cm1)=24 in kappa. It is tier B exact arithmetic but constrains only the ONE combination c(0)+2*c(-1), not the full DMVV structure. Do not oversell this as testing 'the whole product'; Part 2's G_2 identity (4*Delta*psi_1 = 9B^2/A + 3E4*A) is the structural test that uses c(D) for D>4 as well.

m_minus1.status: definitional; no further identity to test per problem statement

m_0.status: holds identically BY CONSTRUCTION (c(D) were defined as the Fourier coefficients of 2B, so G_1:=sum_{s,t} c(4s-t^2) q^s y^t is 2B term-for-term)
m_0.note: definitional: c(D) was extracted FROM B, so G_1 := sum c(D) q^n y^l == 2B identically; not an independent test.

negative_control.purpose: Shows the m=1 identity 4G2=9B^2+3E4A^2 is a genuine, non-tautological consistency check: an arbitrary +1 shift in a single Fourier coefficient c(D) of the K3 elliptic genus breaks it. This is the rigidity evidence for TRACK B: the c(D) table (hence the DMVV structure built from it) admits no 1-integer deformation at D=3 or D=4 that preserves the m=1 identity.

expected_from_literature_UNVERIFIED.note: from memory, Dabholkar-Murthy-Zagier polar-term multiplicity p_24(2)

5_part3_polar_subtraction.support_filter_used: n<=QCHK-2, |l|<=20, D=4n-l^2>=-4 (excludes finite-YCAP-truncation noise in the deep-negative-D tail of 1/A; see note)
5_part3_polar_subtraction.caveat: Truncated at QCHK=5 in q to keep the invA recursion and A_{2,1}/Hhat construction well inside runtime budget; the top q-order (q^QCHK) is dropped from the comparison because the invA recursion's own truncation error concentrates there (finite YCAP and the geometric-series truncation in the s<=-1 / s=0 branches of A_{2,1} both introduce boundary effects at the highest retained order -- reported honestly, not hidden).

could_not_do: Could not push the m=1 (4G2=9B^2+3E4A^2) check or the N/M polar scans to arbitrarily high truncation order within the time budget; verified exactly to q^10 (part 2) and q^4-q^6 with the D>=-4,|l|<=20 support window (part 3). Higher orders were not attempted; no claim is made about them.

The deep-negative-D (D<-4) tail of the polar-subtraction remainder was NOT reconciled -- it carries residual noise from the finite-window (YCAP) truncation used to construct 1/A as a power series, and was excluded from the N/M scans rather than debugged further (documented, not hidden).
psi_{-1} (m=-1) was only recorded definitionally (Delta*psi_{-1}=1/A); no further identity was computed for it since the problem statement gives none to test.
The m=0 check (Delta*psi_0=2B/A) is tautological given how c(D) was extracted from B; flagged, not presented as independent confirmation.
